name: Victorian Sentimental Jewellery
aliases: Sentimental jewels of the Victorian era
summary: Jewels that hold a person or a feeling: lockets, hair work, cameos, snakes, hearts, and black jet for mourning. They were made in gold, jet and pearl in Britain after 1837.

philosophy.core_thesis: A jewel carries a memory: it holds a lock of hair, a name or a likeness close to the body.
design_principles: Give each piece a hollow or a glass front for a lock of hair, a portrait or a monogram.
Carve jet or conch shell by hand into a flower, a hand, a cross or a head in relief.
Make mourning jewellery in black jet for the first year and the first two years of widowhood, with pearls as tears.
Shape the piece as a symbol: a heart, a snake with a tail in its mouth, a clasped hand, an anchor or a forget-me-not.
Engrave a date, a name or a motto on the back of the piece.
Wear a locket on a long chain or a short velvet ribbon, at the centre of the chest or the throat.
Set small stones in a ring so that the first letters of the stones spell a word, such as REGARD.
Fit a brooch with a safety catch and a hinged back, for a pin that holds a shawl or a collar.
anti_patterns: Platinum and white diamond lines of 1905
Bare, plain metal with no message
Bright plastic or paste costume sparkle

silhouette.shape: A medium, hand-sized jewel with a message: an oval locket, a cameo brooch or a bracelet of hair with a gold clasp.
silhouette.line: Oval, round and heart outlines with a bead or a rope edge, kept simple so that the symbol reads.
silhouette.fit: Worn at the throat or the chest on a chain or a ribbon, pinned at the collar, or on the wrist.
silhouette.proportion: A locket is 3 to 5 cm tall. A cameo brooch is 4 to 6 cm wide. A mourning chain is 40 to 90 cm long.
rules: Place a locket on a long chain at the centre of the chest.
Pin a cameo or a jet brooch at the high neck of a dark dress.
Make a bracelet of a gold band with a hinged snake head and a small stone for an eye.
Pair a black jet brooch, a bracelet and a drop earring as a mourning set.

fabrics.rule: Use gold for the frame and an organic or black material for the message: jet for grief, shell for the cameo, hair for the likeness.

methods: hair woven or coiled under a glass front
hollow locket with a hinged back
black enamel borders for a mourning ring
construction.closures: A hinged back and a pin with a safety catch on a brooch; a spring ring on a chain; a bolt ring on a bracelet.
construction.details: A glass or crystal cover over hair, a pearl border, a gold rope or bead edge, a black enamel band and an engraved date.

surface.pattern: Relief of flowers, hands and heads; engraved script and borders of beads or rope.
surface.gloss: Jet and polished gold take a glass-like shine of 60 to 80 GU; mourning pieces keep black and bright.
surface.wear: Jet chips and gold rubs on the edge; a worn locket shows the owner's hand and keeps its meaning.

palette.strategy: Black jet against yellow gold for grief; gold, pearl and soft colour for love.

processes: hand carving of jet and shell
die stamping of cheap pieces in Birmingham
making.scale: Workshops in Whitby, London and Birmingham, and the Italian cameo trade; mass output of cheap pieces after 1850.
making.signs: Tool marks in the carving, a hinged back with an engraved date and a hair or a portrait behind glass.

pieces.form: Black jet brooch carved with a flower
Gold locket with an engraved cover and a lock of hair
Cameo brooch of a head in conch shell with a gold rope edge
Gold snake bracelet with an enamel head
Seed-pearl necklace with a small drop
Gold mourning ring with a black enamel band

positive: gold locket with a lock of hair
snake bracelet with an enamel head
dark Victorian dress with a high collar

canonical_works.work: Whitby jet jewellery worn in the mourning for Prince Albert
Snake engagement ring of Queen Victoria

evidence.title: Mourning brooches containing the hair of a deceased relative. Wellcome L0036197

emotion.target_response: A private, tender and solemn feeling: the viewer reads love or loss in a small object held close.

use_cases: costume design for a Victorian drama
a museum label for a mourning or love token
a heritage locket for a modern wearer
an image prompt for a Victorian portrait
avoid_when: the brief wants platinum and white stones
the brief is bright, playful or modern

modifiers.how: Drop the jet and the hair, use hand-hammered silver, enamel and pale stones, and keep the hand work.
Replace the gold and the jet with platinum and white stones, and keep the oval outline and the pearl.

ornament_level.note: A mourning piece is plain black; a love token carries more carving and pearls.
